question.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(1,4)$ and is concave down on the interval $(0,5).$ If ${f}^{′}(1)=-2,$ estimate the value of $f(0.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=1$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of the function passes through the point $(1,4),$ so we have $f(1)=4.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(1)=-2,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =4+(-2)(x-1) \\  & =4-2x+2 \\  & =-2x+6.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(0.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=0.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.8) & ≈L(0.8) \\  & =-2(0.8)+6 \\  & =-1.6+6 \\  & =4.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave down on the interval $(0,5),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is above the graph near $x=1,$ and therefore we have an overestimate.
